issues.display_title: Issue #736: fix(import): a Mappedin export without kinds/ imports with every object dropped
issues.main_description_html:
square-one-mall.zip imports "successfully" — 2 floors, 369 Information records and 15 categories all land, the review modal is green — but all 780 geometry features are silently discarded. Every floor row reads 0 objects, the editor panel reads All 0, the Map tab reads Total Objects 0, and canvasDataToGeoJson returns an empty FeatureCollection, so nothing draws. Reported as #728.

Measured on development:

parse     -> floors=2  locations=369  buildings=1
             Level 1 (f_5ae882cc…001) geometry = 318 features
             Level 2 (f_5ae8863…002) geometry = 462 features
convert   -> both levels: walls=0 areas=0 shapes=0 points=0 safety=0 doors=0
runImport -> ok, objectCount = 0 and 0

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:248:

const kind = floor.kinds[feature.properties.id];

Every classification branch below it compares kind to a string literal — :251 room/hallway, :264 wall, :278 object, :287 poi — and there is no else. This export ships no kinds/ directory, so parse.ts:124 (readJson<KindsMap>(files, \kinds/${id}.json`) ?? {}) hands convertFlooran empty map,kindisundefined` for all 780 features, and every one is dropped with no counter, no warning and no throw.

The import still reports success because the only emptiness gate is floors.length === 0 && locations.length === 0 (detectSource.ts:70, mirrored at runImport.ts:36). Two floors and 369 locations, so total geometry loss cannot trip it.

This is a second Mappedin export flavour, not a bad file

#727 mall-demo-facility.zip (imports fine) #728 square-one-mall.zip
classifier kinds/f_*.json → wall / room / object / poi cms/layers.json → layer names
geometry 165 LineString + 33 MultiLineString + 55 Polygon + 85 Point Polygon + Point only, zero LineStrings
extras walkable/, nonwalkable/, annotations/ cms/, floorImages/, textAreas/, outdoors.json

Every parser in src/lib/mappedin/ was written against the kinds flavour only. Nothing reads cms/, layers.json, floorImages/, textAreas/ or outdoors.json.

Everything in this export is a polygon at some scale: 9×13 m retail units (Polygon, 140 on L1), up to a 489×502 m site slab (Floor, 1).

Fix

One expression at convert.ts:248, plus a comment naming the simplification:

// This export flavour ships no kinds/ — every feature is a polygon classified by
// cms/layers.json layer name instead, so nothing matched and the whole floor was
// dropped (#728). A kind-less Polygon cannot occur in a kinds-flavour export
// (checked against every bundle in samples/ and #727), so no format sniffing is
// needed: treat it as a room, and keep a Point that a location is anchored to.
// ponytail: coarse on purpose — see "Deliberately not fixed" below.
const kind =
  floor.kinds[feature.properties.id] ??
  (feature.geometry.type === "Polygon"
    ? "room"
    : feature.geometry.type === "Point" && anchorMap.has(feature.properties.id)
      ? "poi"
      : undefined);

Measured with this applied: L1 0 → 278 areas, L2 0 → 432, and 443 of them carry a real tenant name from locations.json ("Simons", "Scotiabank", "Lucky Lotto Centre") through the existing anchor map; the rest fall back to Room N. canvasDataToGeoJson emits {area: 278} flat and {area: 278, ghost-area: 432} stacked, so it renders. All 81 existing tests under src/lib/mappedin and src/lib/mappedin-import still pass.

The Point half is not optional: 12 tenants are anchored only to Point geometry and stay invisible without it — Victoria's Secret PINK, Starbucks (At Indigo), Centre Court, Grand Rotunda, The Food District, Food Central, CIBC ATMs, Canada Post (Inside Shoppers Drug Mart), Raffi Jewellers, Motor Coach Drop-Off & Pick-Up Area, Outdoor, Clip. The 50 pure connection entrances stay dropped, which is correct — they are navigation anchors, not objects.

Nothing downstream needs walls: floorHasGeometry is walls.length > 0 || areas.length > 0, the map's area layers give fill, outline, label and 3D extrusion on their own, and levelBBox grows over areas. An area-only floor is a fully supported shape of a floor — the code just never produced one before.

Deliberately not fixed here

Each is real, measured, and worth its own task rather than being smuggled into a one-expression fix:

  • Doors stay 0. convert.ts:313 requires a connection's entrance to be a LineString; all 50 here (14 door, 11 escalator, 6 elevator, 1 stairs) are Points. A door has no segment to derive from a single point, and inventing one is the wrong-classification failure mode.
  • Coarse classification. 36 thin Wall ribbons, 23 Void openings and the site-wide Floor slab all import as rooms. The app has an exact open-to-below area type that Void should use.
  • 45 duplicate polygons on L2 (21 byte-identical outer-ring groups) import as stacked co-planar twins with duplicate labels and duplicate object rows. directContainment cannot cut equal-area twins.
  • 6 polygons have interior rings that are dropped — convert.ts:253 and :278 read coordinates[0] only. The L2 Wall donut is 96.8% hole.
  • First-paint cost. 710 areas make the first canvasDataToGeoJson take ~0.7–1.7 s (directContainment is O(n²)); it is WeakMap-cached, so later calls are ~70–90 ms.

A layer-name-driven mapping was designed and rejected for now: as drafted it would have deleted 23 named tenants (Exterior Building → skipped: Cineplex, LCBO, Spence Diamonds…) and hidden 35 more (Connections → hallway, which layer-definitions.ts:79 filters out of the label layer). If it is ever built, key it off default-style.json — it sits at the zip root, exists in both flavours, covers 710/710 polygons and carries real per-layer extrusion heights — not off cms/layers.json.

Acceptance criteria

  • Importing square-one-mall.zip shows non-zero objects per floor in the review modal (L1 278, L2 432).
  • The imported floors render on the Map tab — filled, outlined and labelled areas, not an empty canvas.
  • Anchored tenants keep their names and infoId links; the 12 Point-only tenants are among them.
  • The kinds-flavour exports are unchanged: #727 mall-demo and samples/ still import with the same counts as before (the sample-zip.int.test.ts regression net stays green).
  • A test covers a kind-less Polygon becoming an area and a kind-less anchored Point becoming a poi.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Fixed. PR #737 -> development. Commits 5fccd59, f135925.

A kind-less Polygon now reads as a room and a kind-less Point is kept when a location is anchored to it, at the one line every feature passes through. No format sniffing: a kind-less Polygon cannot occur in a kinds export, checked against every bundle in samples/ and #727.

#728 square-one   Level 1  0 -> 292 objects   (278 areas + 14 points)
                  Level 2  0 -> 437 objects   (432 areas +  5 points)
                  443 areas carry a real tenant name via the existing anchor map
#727 mall-demo    Level 1  297 -> 297   unchanged

A second fix the demo forced

With the import working, the floors arrive as areas and no walls — and the 3D pane covered them with "This level has no walls to preview in 3D. Switch to the Editor tab to draw walls." while the floor was drawn underneath it. Editor3DMapView.tsx:375 gated that placeholder on walls.length > 0, but areas extrude on their own through fp-area-extrusion-* and the view already wires hover handlers to those layers. The placeholder now asks for geometry; wall editing still asks for walls, which is right.

This also corrects something stated during the investigation: areas alone do render and extrude, but that panel-level gate short-circuited the whole preview before it mattered.

Verification

Three tests in src/lib/mappedin/__tests__/convert.test.ts — a kind-less Polygon becomes an area keeping its anchored name, a kind-less anchored Point becomes a poi while an unanchored one is dropped, and a kinds export is untouched. Stashing the fix confirms the first two fail without it; the third passes either way, which is the point.

pnpm test 161 files / 1397 passed · pnpm lint 0 errors · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Demo at .playwright-mcp/demo/736/ (gitignored): reads the object count off the review modal and throws if either floor is 0, then ends on the floors rendered in the editor with their tenant names.

Still open, as scoped above

Doors stay 0 (Point entrances), classification stays coarse (Wall ribbons, Void, the site slab all read as rooms), 45 duplicate L2 polygons stack, 6 interior rings are dropped, first paint is ~0.7-1.7 s on 710 areas. All recorded in the body above; each wants the layer names, which is a bigger change than the report needs.

issues.display_title: Issue #745: fix(import): type Void as open-to-below and the site slab as circulation, not rooms (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
In the kind-less Mappedin flavour (#728 square-one-mall.zip), every polygon that is not a wall band imports as type: "room". Two layers are misclassified in a way the app already has an exact type for:

  • 23 Void polygons on L2 (18.9–329.5 m²) arrive as rooms: 23 opaque cream slabs sealing the atrium, 23 Room N labels, 23 marker anchors, 23 patches of penalised-but-walkable grid across a hole in the floor.
  • The site-wide Floor slab (one per floor, 489 × 499 m, 6.7× the next-largest area) arrives as a labelled Room 53 (L1) / Room 40 (L2).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:300-303 special-cases exactly one layer:

const isWallBand =
  !floor.kinds[feature.properties.id] &&
  floor.layers?.[feature.properties.id] === "Wall" &&
  meanBandWidth(boundaries) <= MAX_WALL_BAND_M * PIXELS_PER_METER;

Everything else with a kind-less Polygon falls into the room branch at :284. The importer has never emitted "open-to-below", even though AreaType (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:56) is "room" | "hallway" | "open-to-below" | "wall" and seven readers already honour open-to-below: no floor slab (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:894), no label, no marker, not walkable, excluded from preview lists.

Fix

Generalise the existing special case into one table instead of adding branches beside it. Next to MAX_WALL_BAND_M (convert.ts:254):

/** cms/layers.json layer name -> AreaType, for the kind-less flavour (#736).
 *  "Wall" additionally needs the meanBandWidth guard; the rest are unambiguous. */
const LAYER_AREA_TYPE: Record<string, AreaType> = {
  Wall: "wall",
  Void: "open-to-below",
  Floor: "hallway",   // the site slab IS the circulation surface, not a room
};

Then replace the isWallBand const with:

const layer = !floor.kinds[feature.properties.id] ? floor.layers?.[feature.properties.id] : undefined;
const areaType =
  layer === "Wall"
    ? (meanBandWidth(boundaries) <= MAX_WALL_BAND_M * PIXELS_PER_METER ? ("wall" as const) : undefined)
    : layer
      ? LAYER_AREA_TYPE[layer]
      : undefined;

and swap isWallBand for areaType at its two uses: the else if (isWallBand) name = "" naming branch (:307) so no typed area burns a Room N number, and the spread at :319 → ...(areaType ? { type: areaType } : {}).

AreaType is not currently imported into convert.ts (lines 2-4 import AreaLayer, CanvasData, Category, FloorplanSegment, Information, LevelData, PointAnnotation, SafetyAnnotation, WallLayer) — add it, or this does not compile.

"hallway" for the site slab rather than dropping the feature: src/lib/routing/pathfinder.ts:120-127 derives the corridor/room threshold from the largest walk area, and the slab is that area. Delete it and the mall's circulation loses both its floor and its walkable grid. "hallway" gets the white transition-space fill and drops the label while keeping both.

Not in scope

  • Wall ribbons are already done by 83e7f4d + db2e864 — verified live at 9/9 on L1 and 26/27 on L2. Do not re-open.
  • The 19,346 m² Wall-layer outlier on L2 (68.9 m mean band width) stays a labelled Room 82; it is a donut whose band width is mismeasured — that belongs to the interior-ring task.
  • Parking / Exterior Building features (42 + 3 + 16 per floor) still import as Room N and are what actually makes the editor canvas 2.3× wider than the building (level bbox 1124 × 933 m vs the 489 × 499 m slab). Real, but it needs a product call — drop outdoor site furniture on import, type it, or keep it — so it is deliberately left out.
  • Migrating the layer lookup to default-style.json. It sits at the zip root of all 7 sample exports, agrees with cms/layers.json on every id (0 disagreements, identical coverage) and additionally carries per-layer extrusion heights — but height does not separate Void from Floor (both 0.28618 m), so the layer name stays the only signal either way. Separate M-sized follow-up whose payoff is heights, not classification.
  • No layer-name normaliser. This export spells sibling layers inconsistently across its two floors (Connections/Connection, Washroom/Washroom_1_), but Wall, Void and Floor are spelled identically on both — exact-string match is correct today, and the table makes the next variant a one-line addition.

Acceptance criteria

  • Importing square-one-mall.zip produces 23 areas with type: "open-to-below" on f_5ae8863043cf634695000002 and 0 on f_5ae882cc43cf634695000001 (that floor has no Void layer).
  • The single Floor-layer polygon on each floor imports with type: "hallway" and an empty name — "Room 53" and "Room 40" no longer appear in level.layout.areas.
  • No typed area consumes a room number: the Room N counter drops by 1 on L1 and 24 on L2.
  • No regression from 83e7f4d — wall-typed area counts stay 9 (L1) and 26 (L2), and the 443 anchored tenant names are untouched.
  • The kinds-flavour export samples/1fcf6c9439afd4ed10e6ce1872d7b806a445290d.zip imports byte-identically: 0 areas typed wall, open-to-below or hallway, 194 centreline walls unchanged.
  • convert.test.ts gains a Void-layer case and a Floor-layer case beside the existing wall-band test.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Known residue, not a bug

SelectionToolbars.tsx:226 offers only room / hallway / open-to-below, so a user cannot set or clear "wall" from the editor UI — the type is import-only by design.

Reported as #728 · scoped out of #736.

RESULT

Fixed on feature/745-layer-area-types, commit dd1f32f.

One LAYER_AREA_TYPE table beside MAX_WALL_BAND_M, and the isWallBand const became an areaType that reads it. "Wall" still has to pass the band-width test (that layer also carries the building outline); "Void" and "Floor" are unambiguous. AreaType added to the type import — it was not there, so the patch would not have compiled without it.

Measured on square-one-mall.zip

Level 1  278 areas   wall 9    open-to-below 0    hallway 1    Room N 64 -> 63
Level 2  432 areas   wall 26   open-to-below 23   hallway 1    Room N 168 -> 144

Per layer, at the feature level:

L1  Floor  1/1  -> hallway,        0 Room N
L1  Wall   9/9  -> wall,           0 Room N
L2  Floor  1/1  -> hallway,        0 Room N
L2  Void  23/23 -> open-to-below,  0 Room N
L2  Wall  26/27 -> wall,           1 Room N  (the 19,346 m2 ring, see below)

No typed area burns a room number, the 443 anchored tenant names are untouched, and informationRecords 369 / categories 15 are unchanged.

Kinds-flavour exports are untouched

samples/1fcf6c94… imports 0 typed areas on both levels with its 44 and 220 centreline walls unchanged, because a kinds export ships no layers map and the table is never read. All 12 src/lib/mappedin test files pass unchanged.

Tests

One case added to convert.test.ts beside the existing wall-band test: a Void polygon becomes open-to-below with an empty name, a Floor polygon becomes hallway with an empty name, a polygon on any other layer is still Room N, and the room numbering stays contiguous — which is what proves a typed area consumes no counter. Stashing the fix makes it fail on the first assertion.

Verification

pnpm test 162 files / 1403 passed, 3 skipped · pnpm lint 0 errors · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Residue, as scoped

The single Wall-layer feature still importing as a room is the 19,346 m² ring whose exterior-only band width reads 68.9 m — measuring it across all rings is #747. Parking / Exterior Building features still import as Room N, and the map fit they widen is #749, which this unblocks: the Floor-layer slab is now identified during convertFloor, which is where #749 takes its site-slab area id.

Stale comment cleared while here: the ponytail: coarse by design note claimed wall ribbons, voids and the slab all arrive as rooms, and pointed at a line number the door guard left two commits ago.

issues.display_title: Issue #746: fix(import): drop byte-identical duplicate polygons on the same floor (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
square-one-mall.zip (#728) carries 45 duplicate polygons on Level 2 — 21 groups of byte-identical outer rings. The importer copies every one in, so the floor gets 45 stacked co-planar twins.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

There is no geometry dedupe anywhere on the import path — the only new Set is src/lib/mappedin-import/mergeIntoProject.ts:94, and it dedupes level ids, not geometry. convertFloor pushes one AreaLayer per Polygon feature unconditionally (src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:314).

What actually goes wrong (measured, not assumed)

  1. No hole is ever cut. directContainment requires a strictly larger parent (src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts:522: area[a] <= area[b] → continue). Equal-area twins are neither parent nor child, so cutHoles(boundaries, []) short-circuits (geometry.ts:403) and two identical MultiPolygons are emitted at identical base_height/height.
    Relaxing <= to < is not a fix — containment would stop being antisymmetric (each twin contains the other) and both slabs would be cut away to nothing, on all 7 call sites.
  2. Edit divergence in 3D. Both features land in fp-area-extrusion-active at fill-extrusion-opacity: 0.95 (src/lib/map/layer-definitions.ts:197), so the footprint composites twice and reads a shade off. The geometry is bit-identical, so it is stable, not flickering — the sharp symptom is that renaming / retyping / re-heighting one twin leaves the other extruding the old value at the same z, so the edit appears to half-apply.
  3. Only one twin is clickable. src/lib/map/useMapSelect.ts:82 takes e.features?.[0]; whichever twin MapLibre returns first always wins, its partner is reachable only from the object panel. dedupeAreaIds does not help — the export gives each duplicate its own feature id.
  4. Inflated object counts. objectCountOf counts layout.areas (src/lib/mappedin-import/attachObjectCounts.ts:17), so the wizard's per-floor count is +45 before the project is even staged; in the editor each duplicate becomes its own manual room (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts:37-40) and its own panel row (src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts:173-174).
  5. Silent perf tax — 45 phantom polygons inflate the O(n²) containment solve for nothing.

The ticket's original "duplicate labels" symptom is false. Twins get different names (roomCounter increments per feature, convert.ts:310), and the canvas overlay's greedy declutter drops the second label anyway (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts:412). The honest label symptom is the inverse: one of the two rooms is permanently unlabelled, and the visible name may belong to the twin you did not select. Do not write acceptance criteria around labels — they would pass on unfixed code.

Fix

Dedupe at import time, in convertFloor (src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts), in the room/hallway branch between const ring = feature.geometry.coordinates[0] (:294) and the name block (:305-312) — before ++roomCounter, so room numbering stays gapless.

Key on the raw export ring, which is literally "byte-identical" and costs nothing. Hold const seenRings = new Map<string, AreaLayer>() next to roomCounter (:268):

const ringKey = JSON.stringify(ring);
const twin = seenRings.get(ringKey);
if (twin) {
  if (!twin.infoId && anchor) { twin.infoId = anchor.infoId; if (anchor.name) twin.name = anchor.name; }
  continue;   // ponytail: first-wins; a twin that disagrees on wall-band vs room keeps file order
}

and seenRings.set(ringKey, area) on the push. ~6 lines, one file.

Carrying the anchor across is the one real data-loss case: two locations anchored to the same footprint. AreaLayer holds a single infoId, so the second has nowhere to go — today it lands on a phantom polygon nobody can click, which is strictly worse.

Not at render time. A dedupe in canvasDataToGeoJson would run per frame per level, fix only the map fill, and leave the twins in layout.areas — object panel rows, wizard counts, editor engine rooms and the three uncached directContainment callers all stay wrong. The duplicates exist because the importer copied them in; that is the choke point.

Not in scope

  • The kind === "object" branch (:337) and src/lib/mappedin-editor/convert.ts:135 — neither has a reported duplicate, and the editor flavour stitches rings from a line graph where exact duplicates are far less likely.
  • Tolerance / snapping / near-match clustering. Byte-identical only.
  • Go backend parity: src/app/api/import/mappedin/route.ts proxies the same file to the Go /v1/import/mappedin. If any flow uses that route the Go parser needs the same dedupe or the two diverge — detectSource.ts:9 already flags exactly this. Flag it to backend, do not fix it here.

Acceptance criteria

  • Two features on the same floor with byte-identical outer rings import as one area; the reported export's L2 loses 45 areas (keeps 21) and the wizard's L2 object count drops by exactly 45.
  • Rings differing by any single coordinate — including a 1e-9 nudge on one vertex — both survive.
  • Identical rings on different floors are both kept (mezzanine, stacked floor, void over the room below). The dedupe is per-floor because convertFloor runs per floor.
  • When the dropped twin carries a location anchor and the kept one does not, the kept area ends up with that infoId and name — no Information link lost, informationRecords.length unchanged either way.
  • Room numbering after dedupe is gapless: Room 1..N, no missing numbers.
  • When twins disagree on classification (one on the Wall layer, one a plain room) the first in file order wins — deterministic, asserted, not left to Map iteration luck.
  • All three committed sample exports import byte-identically — no changed expectations in convert.test.ts or sample-zip.int.test.ts (Level 2 stays 14 shapes / 20 pois / 49 doors / 35 information records).
  • One new unit test on the existing fixtures.ts — no new sample zip needed for the test itself.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Verification note

The 45/21 figures come from the reporter's zip, which is not in samples/ — all three committed exports are clean (0 duplicate ring groups across 32 + 16, 132 and 1043 polygons). That makes the fix a provable no-op on every committed sample (a strong regression guard) but means nobody can eyeball the real before/after without adding square-one-mall.zip to samples/. Worth doing while implementing.

Reported as #728 · scoped out of #736.

RESULT

Fixed on feature/746-dedupe-twin-polygons, commit 129b8b7. Stacked on #745 — both edit the same few lines of convertFloor, so it branches off feature/745-layer-area-types rather than fighting a merge.

seenRings: Map<string, AreaLayer> next to roomCounter, keyed on JSON.stringify(ring) of the raw export ring. A repeat is skipped before the counter runs, and the survivor takes the dropped twin's anchor when it has none.

Measured — and the ticket's arithmetic was off

square-one L2   432 areas -> 408    21 duplicate groups collapsed
                Room N 144 -> 120   anchored areas 238 -> 238 (nothing lost)
square-one L1   0 duplicate groups, untouched

The body says "L2 loses 45 areas and keeps 21". Measured: 21 groups spanning 45 features, so 24 areas are dropped and 21 kept — 45 is the number of features involved, not the number removed. informationRecords stays 369.

A provable no-op on everything committed

samples/1fcf6c94…, samples/b7c1feb… and samples/628-hi-rise have 0 byte-identical ring groups on any floor (checked per floor over every Polygon feature), so their imports are unchanged — which is the regression guard the body hoped for.

Tests

Four cases in convert.test.ts, on the existing fixture builder — no new sample zip:

  • two identical rings import as one area, the first is kept, and room numbering has no gap where the twin would have burnt one;
  • a 1e-9 nudge on one vertex keeps both — no tolerance, no snapping;
  • the dropped twin's location link lands on the survivor: name and infoId carried, and the record still resolves;
  • an identical ring on another floor survives — a mezzanine is not a twin (the dedupe is per floor because convertFloor runs per floor).

Stashing the fix fails the first and third.

Verification

pnpm test 162 files / 1407 passed, 3 skipped · pnpm lint 0 errors · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

As scoped

Rooms and hallways only — the kind === "object" branch and src/lib/mappedin-editor/convert.ts have no reported duplicates. First-wins on a twin that disagrees on wall-band vs room, marked with a ponytail: note rather than a resolution rule for an unreported case.

Flag for backend: src/app/api/import/mappedin/route.ts proxies the same file to the Go /v1/import/mappedin. If any flow uses that route, the Go parser needs the same rule or the two importers diverge — detectSource.ts:9 already carries that warning.

issues.display_title: Issue #747: fix(import): measure wall bands across all rings and keep polygon interior rings (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts reads coordinates[0] of every imported Polygon, so interior rings are silently dropped. Present in all three committed samples: 11 multi-ring polygons, hole fraction 1.1 %–15.5 %, all kind room/hallway.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Scope this honestly — the ring drop is mostly harmless today

Measured end to end (parse → convert → areaHoles → cutHoles) on all three shipped zips plus square-one-mall.zip, reconstructing each dropped ring in projected space:

  • All 21 interior rings across the samples are 100 % covered by sibling polygon features on the same floor — features the importer already brings in as separate areas — so the existing nesting machinery cuts the hole anyway. Residual parent slab over the dropped ring is 0.0–0.2 % for 15 of the 21; only 6 leave 6.4–54.1 %, and that residual comes from directContainment picking a tighter parent for the filling room, not from the ring drop as such.
  • The "L2 Wall donut is 96.8 % hole and imports as a full-floor solid block" claim in #736 is wrong on both facts: its exterior ring is 19,346 m² against a 124,303 m² floor slab (~16 % of the floor, not the building outline), and after the existing cut it renders 609 m² of 19,346 — 96.9 % is already cut away by one nested child.

The part that is a real, visible bug is meanBandWidth: convert.ts:303 measures the exterior ring only. On that same donut, exterior-only mean band width is ~84 m (fails the 3 m wall-band test) versus ~1.3 m across all rings (would pass) — so it imports as a labelled Room 82, the third-largest "room" on the floor. It is 1 feature in 36, but it is the one a user actually sees.

Fix

Two parts, small file, one file:

  1. meanBandWidth over all rings (the user-visible half). Signed area of the exterior minus the interiors, perimeter summed over every ring, and call it with the full projected ring list at :303.
    Math.abs / clamp is required, not optional: real data contains a polygon whose interior ring is larger than its exterior (square-one L2 g_660b1d1996c1aa5108fdc4de, Kiosk layer, hole fraction 685 %). A negative width passes <= MAX_WALL_BAND_M * PIXELS_PER_METER unconditionally and would silently type it as a wall band.
  2. Emit each interior ring as its own area. In the room/hallway branch, for each coordinates[i], i >= 1, push an extra AreaLayer with id: \${feature.properties.id}_h${i}`, name: "", projected boundaries and type: "open-to-below". directContainment/areaHolesthen makes it the parent's direct child,cutHolessubtracts it andpolysToMultiCoordswinds it as a hole;open-to-below` draws no slab, no label, no marker and is excluded from routing. ~5 lines.

Do not extend AreaLayer to a ring array. A hole is a nested sibling area in this model — that is its native idiom (src/lib/map/__tests__/geojson-donut.test.ts already locks the behaviour in), and a ring array would force all seven consumers of boundaries to learn a second shape for zero rendering gain.

Do not skip ring-carrying polygons either: on the #736 donut that drops the building's wall outline entirely, which is worse than what happens today.

Not in scope

  • convert.ts:340 (kind === "object" → Shape.points) keeps coordinates[0]. Shape holds one ring and no sample has a multi-ring object — leave a // ponytail: note and revisit when a real export has one.

issues.display_title: Issue #748: perf(geometry): bbox prefilter in directContainment — 1.1 s per edit on a 432-area level (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
directContainment is a full O(n² · v²) solve with no spatial prefilter. On the 432-area level of square-one-mall.zip (#728) it costs ~1155 ms, and on the 278-area level ~442 ms.

The framing in #736 — "first-paint cost, WeakMap-cached so later calls are 70–90 ms" — is wrong in the direction that raises severity: the cache misses on every edit, so this is a per-edit cost, not a one-time paint.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts:514-529 — a double loop whose only prefilter is a scalar area compare (:522 area[a] <= area[b]), so for a floor of similar-sized rooms roughly half of all n² pairs survive. Each survivor calls polygonInsideLoose (:341-346), which ray-casts every vertex of the inner polygon against every edge of the outer with no early exit — it counts all vertices before applying the 60 % majority. Real mall polygons average ~22 vertices.

Three WeakMaps sit in front of it, all keyed on an object every writer replaces:

  • areaHolesCache (geometry.ts:500) — keyed on the areas array
  • ghostPxCache (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:635) — keyed on the level object
  • labelPointCache (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts:25) — keyed on level.layout

Every store writer rebuilds the array with .map(), so all three miss on every edit — including metadata-only edits where nesting provably cannot have changed: src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts:395 (set area type), :432 (link Information), and src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts:244 (modelToLevel, i.e. every committed 2D-editor change).

Three of the seven call sites have no cache at all and pay the full n² to answer about one area: src/components/editor/preview/previewPinUtils.ts:17, src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:79, src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts:45. The other four: geojson-utils.ts:652, :891, useFloorPlanLabels.ts:35, object-markers.ts:52.

Fix — two lines inside directContainment

  1. Precompute a bbox per polygon next to the existing area array.
  2. Reject disjoint-bbox pairs before polygonInsideLoose:
const ba = box[a], bb = box[b];
if (bb[0] > ba[2] || bb[2] < ba[0] || bb[1] > ba[3] || bb[3] < ba[1]) continue;

Free extra: if (area[a] >= parentArea) continue; right after :522 — a candidate that cannot beat the current best parent never needs the containment test.

The disjoint-bbox rejection is conservative and therefore safe with the loose 60 %-majority containment: a vertex inside outer is necessarily inside outer's bbox, so non-overlapping bboxes means zero vertices inside, which can never reach 0.6. An "inner bbox subset of outer bbox" test would not be safe — do not write that one.

Measured with the patch applied on the real export: 1155 ms → 149 ms and 442 ms → 66 ms (7–8×). Synthetic floors show 100–200×, but real mall polygons average ~22 vertices and the site slab / wall bands have bboxes overlapping most of the floor, so the prefilter rejects far fewer pairs. Quote the 7–8× figure, not the synthetic one.

Skip the grid index and the area sort: sorting only reorders the same n² pairs, and a grid index is a data structure for a win the bbox already delivers.

Not in scope, on purpose

  • Finer-grained WeakMap keys, per-area memoisation, rAF-throttling MapWallVertexHandles.tsx:220-241, narrowing src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts:256 to reuse the array when nothing welded.
    Note the honest consequence: at ~149 ms on the worst real level, the cache-key churn is not made irrelevant by this fix — a metadata-only edit still costs ~300 ms across the geojson and label paths. If a profile still shows a stall after this, the throttle is the next-cheapest lever, and finer cache keys after that.
  • polygonInsideLoose's missing early exit — worth ~2× against the bbox's ~7×. Not worth the diff.

Acceptance criteria

  • The three existing directContainment cases in src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/__tests__/geometry.test.ts:107-136 pass unchanged — nesting, tightest-parent tie-break, and the loose/tolerant case keep their current answers.
  • New case in that file: 710 axis-aligned 8-vertex room polygons in a grid plus 4 enclosing containers; the containment result is correct (each container lists exactly the rooms in its quadrant).
  • Same test asserts one directContainment call on that input is under 100 ms (baseline ~2000 ms, post-fix ~10 ms on generated input — 10× headroom, 20× under the regression, so not flaky).
  • Real-export check: the 432-area level of a kind-less import solves in well under half its current time (~1155 ms → ~150 ms measured).
  • Manual check in the map editor on a large import: dragging a wall vertex stays interactive.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Note on the numbers in #736

"710 areas on one level" is the two-level total — directContainment runs per level, so the real worst case is 432 areas on one level. And the "1–2 s per pointermove" figure is not reachable on this export: Editor3DMapView.tsx:375 gates MapWallVertexHandles on walls.length > 0, and a kind-less import has 0 WallLayer walls. On samples that do have walls, the largest level is 91 areas ≈ 20–35 ms per solve. The per-edit and first-paint costs on a 432-area level are the real ones.

Reported as #728 · scoped out of #736.

RESULT

Fixed on fix/748-containment-bbox-prefilter, commit c4dc78e. Not pushed yet.

Two rejections in the pair loop of directContainment, both exact:

  • a bounding box per polygon, skipping pairs whose boxes do not overlap — a vertex inside outer is inside outer's bbox, so disjoint boxes have zero vertices inside and can never reach polygonInsideLoose's 0.6 majority;
  • area[a] >= parentArea — a candidate no smaller than the parent already found was going to be rejected by the assignment guard anyway.

Measured

square-one L1  278 areas   752 ms -> 126 ms   (6.0x)
square-one L2  432 areas  1419 ms -> 189 ms   (7.5x)
628-hi-rise L0  85 areas    28 ms ->   4 ms   (7.4x)
sample1 L0      91 areas    21 ms ->  11 ms
1fcf L2         18 areas    14 ms ->   4 ms

7–8x on real geometry, as scoped — not the 100–200x a synthetic bench suggests. Real mall polygons average ~22 vertices and the site slab and wall bands have boxes overlapping most of the floor, so the prefilter rejects fewer pairs than generated floors do.

Output is unchanged

Containment is identical (deep-equal on the full result) for every level of samples/1fcf6c94…, samples/b7c1feb…, samples/628-hi-rise, samples/sample1/d3a24a27… and both square-one-mall levels, plus 300 randomised fixtures that include exact-area twins.

Tests

Two cases added to src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/__tests__/geometry.test.ts, beside the three existing directContainment ones (which pass unchanged):

  • the safety property — a child with 4 of 5 vertices inside the parent and one spike outside it is still a child. Its bbox is not contained in the parent's, so this fails the moment someone "optimises" the prefilter into an inner-box-inside-outer-box test.
  • 710 rooms in four quadrant containers, asserting every room lands in its own quadrant and the solve stays under 300 ms. Measured ~4.7 s before the prefilter and well under 300 ms after. The rooms deliberately vary in size: equal-area rooms would be pruned by the existing area[a] <= area[b] skip before any containment test runs, which is exactly the case real floors do not have.

Verification

pnpm test 162 files / 1404 passed, 3 skipped · pnpm lint 0 errors · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Not done here

polygonInsideLoose's missing early exit (worth ~2x against this ~7x) stays as scoped. This composes with #751, which removes the n repetition of the same solve — after both, the Directions panel pass on a 432-area level is a few hundred ms.

issues.display_title: Issue #750: perf(routing): Directions freezes the tab for minutes — buildGrid scans every cell against every area (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
Asking for directions on a large venue freezes the tab for minutes. buildGrid scans every grid cell against every walkable area, so its cost is cells × vertices-of-the-polygons-whose-bbox-covers-them.

Measured on the real exported buildGrid (two independent harnesses, node 20 / vitest):

fixture span areas cells @ 4 px grid MB buildGrid
samples/b7c1feb… L0 78 × 46 m 36 0.09 M 0.6 0.22–0.35 s
samples/628-hi-rise L0 139 × 107 m 85 0.38 M 2.5 0.9–1.3 s
samples/1fcf6c94… L1 271 × 455 m 18 3.10 M 20.7 1.8–2.0 s
samples/sample1 L0 255 × 152 m 91 0.97 M 6.5 6.1–7.8 s
square-one-mall L0 1124 × 933 m 278 26.2 M 175 135–165 s
square-one-mall L1 1123 × 932 m 432 26.2 M 175 206–262 s

This is not a Square-One-only defect. A committed 255 × 152 m sample already costs 6+ s, because 99 % of its time is two ordinary hallway polygons whose bounding boxes span the whole plan.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

src/lib/routing/pathfinder.ts:133-154 — a per-cell loop over every walkable area:

for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
  for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
    for (let k = 0; k < walkAreas.length; k++) {
      if (wx < b.x0 || wx > b.x1 || wy < b.y0 || wy > b.y1) continue;
      if (pointInPolygon([wx, wy], walkAreas[k].boundaries) && sizes[k] < smallest) { ... }

The bbox prefilter at :143 works — it cuts surviving pointInPolygon calls to 0.50–1.82 per cell — but each survivor walks the polygon's entire ring. A non-convex 233–566-vertex hallway or site slab has a bbox covering the whole plan, so the prefilter cannot help. The defect is using a bbox as a proxy for a snaking polygon.

Instrumented split (byte-identical replica, verified diff = 0 against the real function): area rasterisation is 99–99.8 % of buildGrid. Wall carve, door carve and clearance are noise. Total polygon-edge steps: 246 M on sample1, 3440 M on SQ1 L0, 4542 M on L1. On L1 a single polygon (Room 40, 124,303 m², 566 vertices) is 74 % of the level; top 3 = 77 %.

When it runs, and what the user gets

Lazy, per route, uncached, synchronous inside React's render:

PreviewOverlay.tsx:200-217 (useMemo, gated at :201/:204-209) → planMultiLevelRoute (src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:181) → routePixels (:96-101) → computeLevelBbox + buildGrid. Nothing else imports buildGrid (only multiLevelRoute.ts:12).

Directions is rendered on every surface — editor preview (src/app/editor/[projectId]/page.tsx:74), preview/[projectId]/page.tsx:52, the public map v/[key]/page.tsx:75 and the embed — and grep finds no cell cap, no area cap, no bail, no fallback anywhere in src/lib/routing/.

Because the work happens in useMemo during render there is no spinner, no paint and no cancel: DirectionPanel.tsx:32-40 has no "computing" state, so the tab simply stops responding and Chrome offers to kill it. Memory is the other half: the grid is 175 MB and findPath allocates a further ~236 MB (g Float32 + parent Int32 + closed Uint8) — ~380 MB for one route on one level, which is a tab OOM on mobile.

It gets worse with a sibling: today SQ1 returns no-connector in 1.9 s only because the importer discards every vertical connector. #744 restores 18 of them, each present on both floors — the :215/:220 loops then call routePixels 36 times, i.e. ~6300 s for one cross-level route.

Fix

1. Scanline fill, replacing pathfinder.ts:133-154 (~18 lines for the 22 removed). Visit areas smallest-first, and for each area walk only the rows of its own bbox: collect edge crossings at wy, sort, fill each span with if (!blocked[i]) continue; blocked[i] = 0; if (isRoom) roomId[i] = k;. First writer wins, which reproduces today's smallest/smallestK rule exactly. sizes, roomThresh and aboxes (:125-132) stay.

Measured, output byte-identical — blocked and roomId diff 0 over 30.7 M cells across five real levels, clearance field diff 0 too:

  • SQ1 L0 154.6 s → 229 ms (676×), SQ1 L1 → ~180-230 ms
  • sample1 7.8 s → 68 ms (115×), 1fcf 1.8 s → 55 ms, 628 1.1 s → 53 ms, b7c1 220 → 15 ms

Route quality cost: none. Same grid bit for bit, so every existing route, door thread and room penalty is unchanged and none of the 24 routing tests move. That is the reason to prefer it over any cell-size change.

The equivalence rests on Array.prototype.sort being stable (today's sizes[k] < smallest breaks ties by array order). Not academic: #746 documents 45 byte-identical polygons on L2, i.e. 45 exact area ties. Use a stable sort and a strict <, and pin it with the DIFF-0 test below.

2. Memoise the grid in routePixels (src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:96-101) — a WeakMap keyed on level.layout.areas, copying the pattern the repo already ships at src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts:500 (areaHolesCache). ~3 lines. Without it, #744's 18 connectors mean 36 grid builds per cross-level route even at 0.2 s each, plus 18 findPath runs allocating 236 MB apiece.

Explicitly deferred

  • Adaptive CELL_PX / cell ceiling. It is a 17-site substitution inside buildGrid, not 3 lines, and it cannot be validated for harm on this export (SQ1 has 0 walls and 0 doors). On the other exports the smallest real door is 0.39 m and the modal doorway 0.91 m; at an 11 px cell the scaled carve capsule is 1.65 m — 1.8× the modal doorway, punching ~0.37 m of wall on each side, exactly the failure pathfinder.ts:184-187 warns about. If the ~380 MB/route OOM needs an answer sooner, the honest guard is refusing to plan above a cell-count limit with a visible "route unavailable", not silently coarsening geometry the user cannot see.
  • Worker thread / navmesh / incremental grid / server-side grids — all rewrites to beat 0.2 s.
  • Sorting areas ascending + break on first hit (the tempting 2-liner that keeps the per-cell loop). Measured: it is slower than today on the two biggest fixtures (sample1 7.4 → 8.6 s), because the break rarely fires on cells no small area covers.
  • Import cleanup alone (#745, #746) does not fix it: #745 types the site slab hallway, and pathfinder.ts:124 filters only open-to-below, so the slab keeps 100 % of its cost.
  • The panel-open freeze (79–266 s before any route) is a different defect in previewPinUtils — filed separately. Do not let two tickets claim the same seconds.

Acceptance criteria

  • buildGrid output is byte-identical to today: blocked and roomId diff 0 on all committed samples and on both square-one-mall levels (30 M+ cells), plus the clearance field.
  • The DIFF-0 test includes a level with exact area ties (SQ1 L1 has 45) so the stable-sort tie-break is pinned, not assumed.
  • buildGrid on the 26 M-cell level completes in well under 1 s, down from 135–262 s; sample1 L0 drops from 6+ s to well under 0.5 s.
  • Two routePixels calls for the same level in one plan build the grid once (WeakMap hit), asserted with a call counter.
  • All 24 existing routing tests pass unchanged — no route result moves.
  • CELL_PX is unchanged at 4.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Numbers to quote

135–165 s (L0) / 206–262 s (L1) and ~676× on the big venue; 14–115× on the committed samples. Earlier probe figures of 162/262 s and "900–1400×" are that harness's high end — do not repeat them.

Reported as #728 · found while scoping #736/#749. Independent of the import fixes; #744 makes it materially worse.

RESULT

Fixed on fix/750-buildgrid-scanline, commit 8278395. Not pushed yet.

buildGrid's area pass is now a scanline fill over each area's own rows, smallest-first, first writer keeps the cell — the same rule the per-cell scan computed with smallest/smallestK, tie-break on array order included. routePixels memoises the grid per level object.

The grid is bit-identical

blocked and roomId diff 0 against a reference copy of the old per-cell algorithm over:

  • 52,441,177 cells — both square-one-mall.zip levels (278 and 432 areas)
  • every level of samples/1fcf6c94…, samples/b7c1feb… and samples/628-hi-rise (17 levels)
  • 948,345 cells across 200 randomised floors (concave rings, 3–11 vertices, forced exact-area twins)
square-one L1  278 areas  26,233,207 cells   157,986 ms -> 1,166 ms   (135x)
square-one L2  432 areas  26,207,970 cells   215,105 ms ->   743 ms   (289x)
1fcf L2         18 areas   3,095,360 cells     1,871 ms ->   123 ms
628-hi-rise L0  85 areas     377,300 cells       948 ms ->    27 ms
b7c1 L0         36 areas      90,783 cells       112 ms ->    11 ms

The new figures are the whole buildGrid including clearanceField; the old ones are the area pass alone, so the real gap is slightly wider.

Grid memoisation

routePixels holds a WeakMap<LevelData, WallGrid>. A cross-level plan with two spanning shafts built 4 grids and now builds 2; replaying the same plan builds 0. Replacing one level object — what any edit does — rebuilds only that level. findPath and nearestPassable only read the grid, so reuse is safe.

Without this, #744's 18 both-floor connectors would turn one cross-level route on this venue into 36 grid builds.

Tests

src/lib/routing/__tests__/pathfinder-grid.test.ts — keeps the old per-cell algorithm as a reference and diffs it cell by cell on a fixture built to exercise every branch: a plan-spanning container, nested rooms, a concave U (two spans per row), byte-identical twins, two different polygons of exactly equal area, vertices on and off the 4 px grid, an open-to-below void and a degenerate 2-point ring. A separate case pins the tie-break (lowest index wins — a <= or an unstable sort flips it, and #746 documents 45 exact ties on square-one L2), one keeps the wall/door carve honest, and one rasterises a 400-vertex plan-spanning ring with 300 nested rooms under 1 s where the old scan needs ~10 s.

src/lib/routing/__tests__/route-grid-cache.test.ts — counts buildGrid calls through planMultiLevelRoute: one per level, zero on replay, one after a level object is replaced.

Verification

pnpm test 164 files / 1408 passed, 3 skipped · pnpm lint 0 errors · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean. The 24 existing routing tests pass unchanged — no route result moved. CELL_PX is still 4.

Not done here, as scoped

The adaptive cell ceiling stays deferred (17 CELL_PX sites, and its widened carve capsule is 1.8x the modal 0.91 m doorway). The panel-open freeze belongs to #751. One robustness note beyond the original scope: the span math clamps to the grid and drops NaN intersects, so a corrupt coordinate cannot spin the fill loops — the old per-cell test simply compared and moved on.

issues.display_title: Issue #751: perf(preview): opening Directions freezes for 79-266 s — one containment solve per pin (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
Clicking the Directions button freezes the tab for 79 s on Level 1 and 266 s on Level 2 of an imported venue — before the user has typed an origin or destination. This is separate from the route computation itself.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:490-493 builds the direction dots by calling findAreaAnchor once per Information-linked area:

...singleLevel.layout.areas
  .filter((a) => a.type !== "hallway" && a.type !== "open-to-below" && informationRecords.some((r) => r.id === a.infoId))
  .flatMap((a) => { const anchor = findAreaAnchor(canvasData, a.id, a.id, singleLevelId); ... })

and each of those calls runs a full containment solve over the whole level — src/components/editor/preview/previewPinUtils.ts:17:

const holes = directContainment(areas.map((x) => x.boundaries))[idx].map((j) => areas[j].boundaries);

That is n × O(n²). The .map also builds a fresh array every call, so no cache keyed on the areas array could ever hit.

Measured: 205 linked areas on L1, 238 on L2; directContainment alone costs 573 ms (278 areas) / 1070 ms (432 areas), giving 78.8 s and 266.2 s for the full set. Same render-phase problem as the routing grid: it runs inside useMemo, so there is no paint, no spinner and no cancel.

Fix

Solve containment once per level, not once per pin. directContainment already returns the answer for every area in one pass — the loop throws away 99.5 % of each result.

Lift the solve out of the per-area call: compute the containment (or the label points directly) once for singleLevel.layout.areas in the directionDots memo and index into it, leaving findAreaAnchor for genuine one-off lookups. Alternatively give findAreaAnchor a batch sibling that takes the ids it needs. Either way the count drops from n solves to 1.

Expected: 205 × 573 ms → one 573 ms solve on L1 (and ~75 ms once #748 lands its bbox prefilter), i.e. minutes → well under a second.

Relationship to #748

Both are needed and they fix different factors:

  • #748 makes each directContainment call ~7–8× cheaper (bbox prefilter inside the function).
  • This task removes the n× repetition. With #748 alone the freeze is still ~15 s on L1 and ~50 s on L2 — better, not fixed.

Land either order; the acceptance numbers below assume #748 has not landed, so re-measure if it has.

Acceptance criteria

  • Opening the Directions panel on a 432-area level runs directContainment once, not once per pin — asserted with a call counter, not a stopwatch.
  • Panel open on square-one-mall L2 drops from ~266 s to under 2 s (under ~0.5 s with #748 landed).
  • The dots themselves are unchanged: same count, same positions, same areas filtered out (hallway, open-to-below, unlinked).
  • findAreaAnchor's existing behaviour for a single lookup is unchanged — it is also used by multiLevelRoute.ts:79 per route endpoint.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Reported as #728 · found while measuring the routing grid. Independent of the import fixes.

RESULT

Fixed on fix/751-direction-pin-anchors, commit 7df0ed3. Not pushed yet.

The solve already had a cached wrapper — areaHoles (#675), keyed on the areas array the caller holds. findAreaAnchor called directContainment(areas.map(...)) directly, and that fresh .map array made the cache unreachable by construction. Routing it through areaHoles makes the whole direction-dots pass one solve plus a labelPoint each.

Measured on the imported square-one-mall.zip, anchors byte-identical:

Level 1  278 areas  205 linked pins   90.5 s -> 843 ms
Level 2  432 areas  238 linked pins  398.4 s -> 1755 ms

(The old figures are extrapolated from three real lookups per level — running all 443 takes ~8 minutes. The issue's 79 s / 266 s were measured on a faster box; the ratio is what matters.)

Same one-line fix at the sibling call sites

Four call sites held a stable level.layout.areas and still called the raw solve. All now share one answer per level:

  • src/components/editor/preview/previewPinUtils.ts:21 — findAreaAnchor, the defect this issue reports
  • src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:79 — areaAnchor, once per route endpoint and once per candidate door on a cross-building plan
  • src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts:35 — label anchors; it had its own labelPointCache, so this only widens the sharing
  • src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:652 — ghost-level geometry, which now shares with :891 and object-markers.ts:52

src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts:45 deliberately stays on the raw call: its polygons come from engine rooms, not from a level's areas array, so there is nothing stable to key on.

Tests

src/components/editor/preview/__tests__/previewPinUtils.test.ts — anchors match a reference built on the old raw-solve path (including a room-in-room donut, where the anchor must land on the ring and not in the hole), active-level scoping and unknown ids still return null, and a 601-area level resolves every anchor under 300 ms. Reverting just the previewPinUtils line makes that last case fail at 2686 ms, so the check is real.

Verification

issues.display_title: Issue #743: fix(import): a Mappedin export whose door entrances are Points imports 0 doors (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
square-one-mall.zip (#728) imports 0 doors on both levels. connections.json holds 32 connections (14 door, 11 escalator, 6 elevator, 1 stairs) and all 50 entrance geometries are Point nav nodes (details.externalId: "NODE-…"), so the door loop drops every one.

Measured at development HEAD (973f32f), per level:

Level 1  walls 0  areas 278  (9 wall bands)  points 14  doors 0
Level 2  walls 0  areas 432  (26 wall bands) points  5  doors 0

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:370:

if (feature?.geometry.type !== "LineString" || feature.geometry.coordinates.length < 2) continue;

A door is FloorplanSegment — {x1, y1, x2, y2} (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:78-90), two endpoints and no host-wall id. A single Point has no segment, so there is genuinely nothing to derive at that expression.

The doorway geometry is in the export, just not where the loop looks

cms/layers.json puts 24 polygons on an "Entrance" layer (11 on L1, 13 on L2), mean band width 0.639–1.069 m — the same ribbon signature meanBandWidth already tests for on the "Wall" layer. All 14 door entrance Points land within 1.26 m of an Entrance ribbon edge (median 0.425 m ≈ half a band width, i.e. on its centreline); 11 of the 14 sit strictly inside a ribbon.

Today those 24 ribbons fall through the kind-less-Polygon branch at convert.ts:284 and import as areas: 15 as bogus Room N, and 9 with the real name Entrance plus an infoId.

Fix

All inside convertFloor, src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:

  1. Collect the bands. Mirror the existing isWallBand test (:300-303) with isDoorBand: kind-less Polygon, floor.layers?.[feature.properties.id] === "Entrance", meanBandWidth(boundaries) <= MAX_WALL_BAND_M * PIXELS_PER_METER. Push the projected ring onto a local doorBands: number[][][]. Skip the areas.push only when the ribbon has no anchor — 9 of the 24 are location-anchored, and skipping those would silently drop 9 Information links.

  2. Replace the guard at :370 with a two-branch read of feature.geometry.type:

    • LineString / MultiLineString — unchanged, the #428 flavour must keep its 8/49 doors;
    • Point — project it, scan the doorBands edges for the nearest, and if it is within 1.5 * PIXELS_PER_METER push that edge verbatim as the door. Nothing near ⇒ continue, as today.

    Use a local nearest-edge loop or nearestOnSegment; distToSegmentSq at src/lib/routing/pathfinder.ts:98 is module-private, not exported.

    The ribbon edge verbatim, not a synthesized centreline: the ~0.45 m offset is inside wallOpenings' 0.6 m tolerance, and a farthest-vertex-pair centreline is wrong on the 7 bent/L-shaped ribbons (it holds for only 17 of 24).

  3. src/lib/mappedin/types.ts:80-83 — add id?: string and details?: { name?: string } to ConnectionEntry. All 14 door connections carry both ("Food District Entrance", "Entrance with Walmart", "Underground Parking Entrance 1").

No fallback stub at the Point. A floating 1 m door with invented orientation is worse than no door, and every Point in this export has a band within 1.26 m.

What this buys — and what it does not

Do not accept this on "the doorway is cut into the 3D wall". You cannot see that here, and it is not this task's fault: this export produces zero WallLayer walls (its walls are ribbon polygons imported as type: "wall" areas) and src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:843 only cuts openings into layout.walls.

The demonstrable payoff is:

  • Outdoor routing can enter the building. The shell is built from all 278 ground-floor area rings and buildOutdoorGrid carves only doors back out (src/lib/routing/pathfinder.ts:274-286) — with 0 doors the mall is sealed to every cross-building route.
  • 14 named, selectable, Information-linkable entrance markers and object rows (src/lib/map/object-markers.ts:63-66 anchors a door marker at its midpoint).
  • Fewer bogus Room N labels.

Not in scope

  • The 18 escalator / elevator / stairs connections dropped by if (conn.type !== "door") continue; (convert.ts:366) — separate task.
  • Turning wall bands into WallLayer centrelines (skeletonisation), explicitly declined in #736.

Acceptance criteria

  • An integration check over square-one-mall.zip reports 14 doors across the two levels (11 + 3) where HEAD reports 0.
  • Every imported door segment has non-zero length and its midpoint is within 2 m of the connection's entrance Point after the projection pipeline.
  • Doors carry the connection name — at least one imported door has name === "Entrance 3 with Harry Rosen".
  • No area is named Room N while its cms/layers.json layer is "Entrance"; the 9 anchored Entrance ribbons keep their name and infoId.
  • src/lib/mappedin/__tests__/sample-zip.int.test.ts passes unchanged — 8 doors on Level 1, 49 on Level 2 for the LineString flavour.
  • convert.test.ts keeps its existing door cases and gains a Point-entrance case plus a Point-with-no-nearby-band case that must still import 0 doors.
  • The stale (see :313) reference in the comment at convert.ts:283 is corrected — the guard now lives at :370.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Verification note

square-one-mall.zip is not in samples/ — it lives only in .playwright-mcp/demo/736/ (gitignored). Add it to samples/ while implementing, or the integration check above cannot run in CI.

Reported as #728 · scoped out of #736.

RESULT

Fixed on feature/743-point-door-entrances, commit d0bfb9d. Stacked on #757 (#747) — both edit the band-width call site.

doorBands collects the projected "Entrance"-layer ribbons while the geometry loop runs; the door loop then snaps a Point entrance onto the nearest band edge within 1.5 m, and adds nothing when none is near.

Measured

square-one L1  0 -> 8 doors, 2.7-11.1 m, all named
square-one L2  0 -> 6 doors, 1.9-9.0 m, all named
               areas 278 -> 270 and 408 -> 401 (the 15 unanchored ribbons)
               anchored areas 205 / 238 unchanged, informationRecords 369 unchanged
1fcf sample    8 and 49 doors, unchanged
628-hi-rise    unchanged

14 doors, one per door connection, none degenerate. Names come from connections.json — "Food District Entrance", "Simons Entrance", "Entrance 8 with Sport Check". Zero Room N areas remain on the Entrance layer, and the 9 anchored ribbons keep their name and infoId.

Decisions worth reviewing

  • The edge verbatim, not a centreline. The ~0.45 m offset is inside wallOpenings' 0.6 m tolerance, and a farthest-vertex-pair centreline is wrong on the bent, L-shaped ribbons — it holds for only 17 of the 24.
  • Nothing near ⇒ no door. A floating door of invented orientation is worse than no door, and every Point in this export has a band within 1.26 m.
  • The ribbon is dropped only when unanchored. 9 of 24 carry a location; dropping those would lose 9 Information links.
  • ConnectionEntry.details.name is added here for the door name. #758 (#744) adds the same field for access-point names — whichever lands second will have a one-line conflict in types.ts.

What this does not buy

Do not accept on "the doorway is cut into the 3D wall". This export produces zero WallLayer walls — its walls are ribbon polygons typed type: "wall" areas — and geojson-utils.ts:843 only cuts openings into layout.walls. The payoff is outdoor routing being able to enter the building at all (buildOutdoorGrid carves only doors out of the ground-floor shell), plus 14 named, selectable, Information-linkable entrances.

Tests

Three cases in convert.test.ts: a nav node on a band's centreline produces one named door with a non-zero span; a nav node 50 m from any band produces none; and the ribbon is dropped unless anchored, in which case it keeps its name and infoId and still yields the door. The first and third fail with the fix stashed.

Verification

issues.display_title: Issue #744: feat(import): read escalator, elevator and stairs connections as Access points (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
An imported Mappedin export produces 0 access points, so a multi-level import has no way to move between floors. square-one-mall.zip (#728) ships 18 vertical connections — 11 escalator, 6 elevator, 1 stairs, 36 entrance Points in total — and every one is discarded on import.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:366:

if (conn.type !== "door") continue;

The connections loop only ever considers door. Escalator, elevator and stairs connections never reach any writer, and level.accessPoints comes out undefined on every imported level.

Why this one is a pure mapping, not geometry invention

Unlike doors (which need a segment — see the sibling door task), an AccessPoint is a single point, which is exactly what the export gives:

// src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:147-160
export interface AccessPoint extends CreatedAt {
  id: string; x: number; y: number;
  accessId: string;            // group id — members across floors share it
  type: AccessTypeKey;         // "lift" | "stairs" (+ legacy "entrance")
  name?: string; infoId?: string;
  accessOriginLevelId?: string;
}
  • x, y ← the entrance Point, through the same project(...) every other feature uses.
  • accessId ← conn.id, which groups the same lift across floors for free — that is precisely what spansFloors (src/lib/floorplanEditor/accessTypes.ts:36) expects.
  • accessOriginLevelId ← the first floor the connection appears on.
  • name ← conn.details.name.

Requires the same ConnectionEntry widening as the door task (src/lib/mappedin/types.ts:80-83: add id?, details?: { name?: string }).

The one product call

ACCESS_TYPES (src/lib/floorplanEditor/accessTypes.ts:9-12) has exactly two authorable keys — lift and stairs. There is no escalator key, and entrance is legacy/read-only.

So the 11 escalators must fold into one of the two. Recommended: lift (both are powered vertical transport, both span floors, spansFloors treats them the same). Do not add a third AccessTypeKey for this — that pulls in an icon, a colour, a picker entry and the accessIcons.tsx exhaustiveness check for zero routing gain.

Acceptance criteria

  • Importing square-one-mall.zip yields non-empty accessPoints on both levels; the 18 vertical connections produce access points (11 escalator + 6 elevator → lift, 1 stairs → stairs).
  • Connections that appear on both floors share one accessId, so the pair reads as one connected object and multi-level routing can use it.
  • Each access point sits at its entrance Point in canvas px and carries conn.details.name when the export has one.
  • door connections still import as doors, unchanged; a connection with no entrance geometry is still skipped.
  • AccessTypeKey is untouched — no new key added.
  • Unit test in src/lib/mappedin/__tests__/convert.test.ts covering escalator → lift, stairs → stairs, and cross-floor accessId grouping.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Reported as #728 · found while scoping the door half of #736.

RESULT

Fixed on feature/744-vertical-connections-access, commit b9624ef.

VERTICAL_ACCESS_TYPE maps elevator/escalator -> lift and stairs -> stairs, and a second loop over connections emits one AccessPoint per entrance on the floor being converted. ConnectionEntry gained id and details.name.

Measured

square-one    0 -> 18 per floor (17 lift, 1 stairs), all named,
              18 accessId groups, every one spanning both floors
1fcf sample   0 -> 5 (L1) and 8 (L2)
628-hi-rise   0 -> 6..16 per floor

A cross-level route now resolves. planMultiLevelRoute from "Lucky Lotto Centre" (L1) to an L2 tenant returns status: "found", 2 segments, 1 transfer — where before it returned no-connector, because the importer had discarded every connector.

One thing the issue did not call out

rotateLevels, translateLevels and bboxOf did not carry accessPoints. Without adding them the markers would sit at unrotated, unshifted coordinates while every other object moved — the import pipeline rotates the building to its dominant wall axis and then shifts it into positive canvas space. A test pins it: an entrance sharing a coordinate with a room vertex must land on that vertex's pixel after the whole pipeline.

Escalators fold into lift

ACCESS_TYPES (accessTypes.ts:9-12) has exactly lift and stairs; entrance is legacy and read-only. A third key would need an icon, a colour, a picker entry and the accessIcons exhaustiveness check, for no routing gain — both are powered vertical transport that spans floors identically. AccessTypeKey is unchanged.

Tests

Four cases in convert.test.ts: elevator/escalator -> lift and stairs -> stairs with a missing-geometry connection still skipped; cross-floor accessId grouping plus accessOriginLevelId and the connection name; the marker landing on the same pixel as a room vertex it shares a coordinate with; and doors still importing as doors, with no door becoming an access point. All four fail with the fix stashed.

Verification

pnpm test 163 files / 1422 passed, 3 skipped · pnpm lint 0 errors · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Follow-up this exposes (not fixed here)

The cross-level route takes 51 s on this venue. The grid work is now cheap (#750 builds each level once, ~1.2 s and ~0.7 s), so what remains is findPath: multiLevelRoute.ts:215-222 runs A* for every connector pair — 18 shafts x 2 legs = 36 runs on 26 M-cell grids, with no pruning by straight-line distance and no early exit once a leg already beats the best score. Worth its own issue; before this fix the loop never ran at all, so the cost was invisible.

issues.display_title: Issue #749: fix(map): an imported site frames the parking lot, not the building — fit is 2.3x too wide (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
Opening the Map tab on an imported Mappedin site frames the parking lot, not the building. square-one-mall.zip (#728) fits to 1123.9 × 933.2 m for a 489.3 × 499.5 m mall — 2.30× too wide, 1.87× too tall, so the building occupies 23 % of the viewport area.

Same cause in the 2D editor: the canvas is sized 23597 × 19598 px against a 9786 × 9990 px mall.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Measured

levelBBox (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:244-259) grows over layout.walls + layout.areas only → levelsLngLatBBox (:433-456) → getBuildingLngLatBounds (:464-481) → map.fitBounds (src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx:139-142, PreviewOverlay.tsx:271, :295, :543-544).

The site slab is the one Floor-layer polygon per floor: L1 489.3 × 499.5 m, L2 491.6 × 485.9 m. Everything past it is outdoor site furniture imported as ordinary areas:

layer L1 L2 features outside the slab max distance out
Parking Lot 42 41 39 / 39 548 m
Exterior Building 16 16 16 / 16 490 m
Parking Garages 3 3 1 / 2 83 m

The eight extent-setting features, measured: Cineplex Parking, Room 23, LCBO, Room 26 (L1); Room 76, Room 82, LCBO, Parking 3 (L2). Three of the eight are location-anchored, which is why no "drop the unnamed ones" rule can fix the extent.

Why the obvious fixes are wrong — all measured, none guessed

  • Drop the three outdoor layers. Orphans exactly 23 of 369 locations, none of which has a second anchor anywhere: 12 tenants (Cineplex, LCBO, Whole Foods Market, Spence Diamonds, Panera Bread, Crate & Barrel, Popeyes, Boston Pizza, Scaddabush, Jack Astor's, Hibachi Teppanyaki & Bar, Space Explorers) and 11 parking facilities. Their Information records survive convertLocations but lose polygon, infoId link, map label and 3D slab. This is the exact regression #736 rejected — and it does not even work: the union only falls to 761.6 × 639.3 m, still 1.56× the slab, because leasing (26 features, up to 186 m out) and one 19,346 m² Wall-layer polygon on L2 remain.
  • Drop only the unanchored ones. 0 tenants lost, but the extent barely moves — union stays at ~95 % of today, for the anchored-extremes reason above.
  • Type them hallway / open-to-below / route them to Shape. All three hide the names: the label layer skips hallway and open-to-below (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts:39) and shapes carry no map label at all. Same rejected failure mode.
  • A per-area outdoor?: boolean flag. Dies on the user's first editor edit. modelToLevel (src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts:196-240) rebuilds every area as { id, name, createdAt, boundaries, height, type: pa?.type, infoId: pa?.infoId } — only type and infoId survive by id. Measured round-trip: flags 72 → 0 (L1) and 102 → 0 (L2), fit box back to 1123.6 × 932.8 m, and the 2 s autosave persists the flag-less version. Level-level fields survive (modelToLevel returns { ...prev, layout }); per-area fields are projected away.

The product call this ticket is actually asking for

Framing the mall pushes the protected tenants off the initial viewport: measured from a 491.7 × 502.2 m fit with padding: 80 px, Cineplex sits 370.5 m outside, LCBO 241.9 m, Whole Foods 42.3 m — 15 of the 23 on L1 and 11 on L2 are entirely off-screen at first paint. "Frame the building" and "show the outparcel tenants" are in direct tension. They stay clickable, labelled and searchable either way; this is only about where the camera starts.

Recommendation: frame the building. A user opening an indoor map expects the indoor map. Say it in the RESULT rather than claiming zero cost.

Fix — at the fit, not in the geometry

  1. During convertFloor, record the site-slab area id on the level, not on each area — one optional field on LevelData (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:271-279, beside mapTransform / buildingId). #745 already identifies the Floor-layer polygon, so this is a by-product of work that is already scoped.
  2. In levelsLngLatBBox (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:433-456), prefer that area's own box when the field is set; fall back to levelBBox(level) otherwise.

~5 lines, survives the editor round-trip, keeps every area, name, label, marker and object row byte-identical to today.

Do not touch levelBBox itself. It has six consumers beyond the camera — computeBBox → makePixelRotator (the pivot the whole model rotates and scales about), levelBBoxCenter → makeLevelLocalTransform and buildingBBoxCenter, repivot (:193, which rewrites a persisted mapTransform when that centre moves), floorSnap.ts:86/:121, and buildingSolidsPx/outdoorGeoJson. Narrowing it would silently move the placement pivot by 231 m east / 78 m south on L1.

Sequencing — do this last

Blocked behind #745 (owns the Floor slab and the layer table that identifies it) and best re-measured after #743, #744, #746, #747: every one of them changes the counts quoted above, and #747 fixes the 19,346 m² Wall polygon that is part of the excess for free. Land those, re-measure, and if the fit is already acceptable close this as fixed-by-siblings.

Not in scope

  • Editor 2D canvas sizing (src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts:99-115). Narrowing it needs convert.ts:412's translation reworked in the same change or the outdoor areas land off-canvas.
  • Routing. buildGrid is timed at 151.9 s (L1) and 206.0 s (L2) on 26.2 M-cell / 78.7 MB grids — and still 86.9 s / 129.5 s with every outdoor feature removed. That is a pathfinder scaling problem (CELL_PX = 4 over a 500 m building), not an extent problem. Separate issue.
  • Dropping, retyping or renaming any outdoor feature.

Acceptance criteria

  • getBuildingLngLatBounds on the imported square-one-mall.zip spans ≤ 505 × 510 m (measured target ≈ 491.7 × 502.2 m), down from 1123.9 × 933.2 m.
  • Round-trip test, mandatory: levelToModel → modelToLevel → re-measure the box, and it is unchanged. This is where the per-area-flag design died and no other criterion catches it.
  • Nothing is dropped or renamed: 369 informationRecords, 15 categories, and per-level area/object counts identical to whatever the sibling tasks leave them at.
  • All 23 outdoor-only locations still resolve to an area with a matching infoId and still emit a label point — assert by name for at least Cineplex, LCBO, Whole Foods Market, Spence Diamonds, Cineplex Parking and "Parking 5 (Underground)".
  • levelBBox has no diff, and neither do computeBBox, makePixelRotator, repivot, floorSnap.ts, buildingSolidsPx or outdoorGeoJson.
  • A level with no site-slab field framed exactly as today — the kinds-flavour exports in samples/ have no Floor layer, so sample-zip.int.test.ts passes unchanged.
  • Unit test on a fixture level: slab area + one far-outside anchored area; the fit equals the slab box, the outside area keeps its name and infoId.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Reported as #728 · scoped out of #736. Blocked behind #745.

RESULT

Fixed on fix/749-frame-the-building, commit f67890b.

LevelData.siteAreaId names the area that is the building footprint; convertFloor sets it from the Floor-layer slab #745 already identifies; getBuildingLngLatBounds prefers that area's box.

square-one   1116 x 927 m -> 488 x 496 m     2.30x the slab -> 1.00x

Nothing is dropped, retyped or renamed: 369 information records, 443 anchored names, every area still drawn, clickable and labelled. Only where the camera starts changes.

The round trip, which is where the first design died

modelToLevel rebuilds every area from a fixed field list, so the per-area outdoor flag went 72 -> 0 and 102 -> 0 on one edit and the fit snapped back. Level fields ride along on { ...prev }. Measured on the real export through levelToModel -> modelToLevel: siteAreaId survives and the fit stays 488 x 496 m. A committed test pins it.

Deliberately narrow

levelBBox is untouched — it also drives makePixelRotator's pivot, the per-building placement centre, repivot's rewrite of a persisted mapTransform, the floor-stack snap and the outdoor shell. Only getBuildingLngLatBounds passes the new preference; buildingIdAtLngLat still hit-tests the full footprint, so a click on the apron still finds its building.

The framing call, stated

15 of the 23 tenants anchored only to outdoor geometry now start outside the initial viewport — Cineplex 370 m out, LCBO 242 m, Whole Foods 42 m. They remain drawn, named, clickable and searchable. This is the product decision this ticket asked for, taken as recommended (frame the building), and it is one line to reverse.

Tests

src/lib/map/__tests__/site-framing.test.ts — the fit frames the building not the apron; it survives levelToModel -> modelToLevel; a siteAreaId pointing at a deleted area falls back to the whole level; and levelBBox plus building hit-testing stay on the full footprint. Plus one assertion in convert.test.ts that the import sets siteAreaId from the Floor layer. The first two fail without the fix.

Verification
