Still open, as scoped

The 2D editor canvas is still sized over every area (bridge.ts:99-115); narrowing it needs convert.ts's translation reworked in the same change or the outdoor areas land off-canvas.

issues.display_title: Issue #759: perf(routing): a cross-level route runs A* for every connector pair — 51 s on an imported mall (#728)
issues.main_description_html:
A cross-level route on an imported mall takes 51 s. The grid is no longer the problem — #750 builds each level's grid once (~1.2 s and ~0.7 s on this venue) — what remains is findPath: the pair loop runs A* for every connector pair, on 26 M-cell grids, with nothing pruned.

Measured on square-one-mall.zip after #744 restored its 18 vertical connectors: 18 shafts × 2 legs = 36 A* runs for one route.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:226-255:

for (const originConnector of spanning) {
  const arrivalPool = arrivals.filter((ap) => ap.accessId === originConnector.accessId);
  for (const destinationConnector of arrivalPool) {
    const firstLeg = routePixels(fromLevel, fromAnchor.point, [originConnector.x, originConnector.y]);
    const secondLeg = routePixels(toLevel, [destinationConnector.x, destinationConnector.y], toAnchor.point);
    ...
    const score = pathLength(firstLeg) + pathLength(secondLeg) + 50;
    if (!best || score < best.score) best = { score, route };

Every candidate is fully solved before it is scored, and the score is thrown away for all but one. There is no ordering, no bound and no early exit. A lift on the far side of the mall costs exactly as much to evaluate as the one twenty metres away.

The cost per run is the grid, not the geometry: A* on the 26 M-cell level drains a large share of it, and a leg with no route drains all of it (measured 20.7 s for one such run on Level 2).

Fix

Branch and bound on a straight-line lower bound. score is pathLength(firstLeg) + pathLength(secondLeg) + 50, and pathLength is geometric length, so the Euclidean distance through a connector is an admissible lower bound — a grid path can never be shorter than the straight line.

For each candidate pair compute

bound = dist(fromAnchor.point, origin) + dist(destination, toAnchor.point) + 50

sort the pairs by bound ascending, and inside the loop break as soon as bound >= best.score. Roughly ten lines around the existing loop; no change to routePixels, findPath or the grid.

It is exact, not a heuristic. Any pair whose bound already exceeds the best score cannot beat it, so the route returned is identical. When nothing routes, best stays null, the bound never prunes, and the blocked-walk / no-connector statuses are reached exactly as they are today.

Expected: 36 A* runs down to a handful — the nearest connector usually wins, and every later candidate is cut by the bound.

Not in scope

  • Caching findPath results, a worker thread, a navmesh, or hierarchical routing. The bound is a ten-line change; revisit only if a profile still shows a stall.
  • The remaining per-run cost on a 26 M-cell grid. The adaptive cell-size ceiling was deferred in #750 for reasons that still hold (17 CELL_PX sites, and its widened carve capsule is 1.8× the modal 0.91 m doorway).
  • planAcrossBuildings (:335, :346) runs a whole planMultiLevelRoute per candidate door. Same shape of problem, and the same bound would apply — but measure it before assuming, and file it separately.

Acceptance criteria

  • A cross-level route on a venue with many shafts calls findPath a small number of times, not once per connector pair — asserted with a call counter on a fixture with 6+ spanning shafts, not with a stopwatch.
  • The route returned is identical to today's on every existing routing test — same segments, same transfer, same connector chosen.
  • A fixture where the nearest connector is blocked still finds the route through a farther one (the bound must not prune a candidate that is merely worse than an unreachable one).
  • no-connector, missing-destination-connector and blocked-walk are unchanged, including the case where no pair routes at all.
  • End-to-end on square-one-mall.zip: a cross-level route completes in a few seconds where it now takes 51 s.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Found while verifying #744 — before it, the importer discarded every connector, so this loop never ran and the cost was invisible. Reported as #728.

RESULT

Fixed on fix/759-connector-pair-bound, commit 2c3375e.

Candidate pairs are built with a straight-line bound, sorted, and the loop breaks at the first bound that cannot beat the best score.

square-one, tenant on L1 -> tenant on L2   51.4 s -> 4.2 s   (12x), same route,
                                           same transfer ("Escalator 5")

What is left is 2 grid builds (~1.9 s) and 2 A* runs — the 36 A* passes are gone.

Exactness

A pruned pair's bound already exceeds the best score, and pathLength is geometric length, so its real score cannot be lower. While nothing has routed yet best is null and nothing prunes, so blocked-walk, no-connector and missing-destination-connector are reached exactly as before.

Tests

src/lib/routing/__tests__/route-connector-bound.test.ts counts findPath calls through planMultiLevelRoute:

  • four spanning shafts, nearest serves both endpoints — 2 calls, not 8;
  • both endpoints at the far end, so the winner is the shaft the old loop reached last — still chosen, still 2 calls (the break must not cut off the true winner);
  • the origin floor split into two disjoint slabs with the nearest shaft stranded on the far one — the route falls through to the reachable shaft, because nothing may be pruned while no route has been found;
  • no-connector and missing-destination-connector unchanged.

The first two fail with the fix stashed (8 calls instead of 2). The 30 existing routing tests pass unchanged — no route result moved.

Verification
